name: pipeline-classification

protocol.note: run_pipeline_classification compiles a real state matrix twice. Compute axis: a tiny SampleFacet kernel specialized by the vg_checked_profile function constant (PipelineKey) crossed with threadgroup width (DynamicState) and sample lod (ShaderVisibleData) -- 2x2x2. Raster axis: MTLRenderPipelineState keyed by attachment pixel format (RGBA8Unorm/R32Float) and sample_count (1/4), crossed with the same dynamic/shader-visible pair (viewport / tint) -- 2x2x2x2. naive-full-permutation creates one MTLComputePipelineState or MTLRenderPipelineState per tuple. vg-stateblock-classification keys only the 06 §7 PipelineKey axes (checked on/off for compute; format×sample_count for raster), so dynamic/shader-visible permutations must hit the cache. UnsupportedNeedsConversion blocks are rejected rather than silently folded into a key. Attachment format and sample count are compiled into the render PSO and therefore key state; viewport and tint must not enlarge it.

correctness.oracle: arithmetic: classified_pipeline_count < naive_pipeline_count; cache_hits>0; cache_misses>0; unsupported_rejected. After the PipelineKey sha256 digest distinguishes attachment format and sample count, the matrix is classified=6 (2 compute checked on/off + 4 raster format×sample) and naive=24 (8 compute + 16 raster). Assert those exact counts when the run matches; otherwise keep the inequalities and record the observed counts rather than inventing a match.

judgement: StateBlock classification on the compute and raster creation paths reduces the test-matrix PSO count below the naive full permutation: dynamic/shader-visible axes hit the classified cache, and an UnsupportedNeedsConversion block is rejected. Per ADR-030 this experiment is a roadmap work item and is implemented, but it is NOT a hard gate for Phase C closure (the catalog Representation gate row lists only E005/E008/E016). Scope includes both compute PSO (checked-profile specialization) and raster PSO (format × sample_count). Compile-time nanoseconds are host-measured per run and are not recorded as a fixture here.
